extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH-style grant applications (vertebrate animal section), grant reviewers, and institutional oversight committees
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing/describing the vertebrate animals, ethical justification, methods to minimize pain/distress, sample sizes, and compliance for an NIH-style research grant studying biofilm infections in mice. Includes collaboration structure, timeline, and contingency plans for experimental risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of hypothesis risk and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: This hypothesis ... carries a measure of risk, since very little is known about how biofilms evade the host immune system, and because these types of measurements are new and new protocols will have to be developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agarose and polyacrylamide gels resist phagocytosis despite provoking an immune response, we will first test whether they are too stiff, and/or have yield stress too high, for neutrophils to overcome. To extend the range of mechanics assayed to softer, weaker materials, we will use alginate and other hydrogels with moduli that are tunable even lower. Should we find that, even in this case, mechanics do not contribute to immune evasion, we would use AFM and shear flow to measure the strength of adhesive forces between neutrophils and biofilms with different polysaccharide production patterns. We anticipate that stronger adhesion between neutrophils and the biofilm target will be linked to a greater probability of phagocytosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline mapping aims to activities across years
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline: Year 1–Year 4 mapping of Aims to Activities (table showing which activities for Aim1/Aim2/Aim3 occur in which years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a year-by-year schedule (e.g., Aim 1 Activity 1 & 2 in Year 1; Aim 2 Activity 1 in Year 2; Aim 3 Activity 1 in Year 2, etc.) to demonstrate planned progress and resource allocation across the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the collaboration and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: P.I. Vernita Gordon will lead the collaboration and coordinate efforts. She will directly supervise image analysis of biofilm structure and wound transport properties (Activities 1-1&2) and in vitro determination of the effects of structure on antibiotic resistance and virulence (Specific Aim 2) and the impact of mechanics on phagocytosis (Activities 3-1&2). Collaborator Kendra Rumbaugh will supervise animal work in Specific Aim 1 and Activity 3-3. Collaborator Gordon Christopher will supervise ex vivo measurements of biofilm mechanics in Activity 1-3. Collaborator Jason Shear will supervise µ3D-printing experiments in Activity 2-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies supervision responsibilities, communication cadence (students and senior personnel meet in person at least yearly; Skype meetings at least monthly), reporting (students prepare written reports bimonthly for distribution to all senior personnel), and evidence of collaboration (joint manuscript under review). Use clear assignment of tasks and regular reporting/meetings to show management and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinded studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Blinded studies: the bacterial strains used will be coded so that researchers at Texas Tech (Rumbaugh, Christopher) will not know which strains were used until experiments and analysis are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coding to blind experimenters/analysts to strain identity to reduce bias in experimental conduct and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of host biological variables and scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible that characteristics of the mouse host, such as strain, sex, and age, may impact our findings. However, the focus of the present study is on characterizing bacterial behaviors and properties and it is outside the scope of this study to examine all the host factors that might impact this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge potential confounders (host strain, sex, age) and explicitly state scope limitations; justify exclusion of exhaustive host-factor analysis when primary focus is bacterial behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with NIH Guide and IACUC approval
rubrics_metrics.description: All experiments will be carried out in strict accordance with the recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals of the National Institutes of Health. The protocol was approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (Protocol Number: 07044).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State adherence to NIH guidelines and include IACUC protocol approval/number to demonstrate institutional oversight and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of proposed use of animals (species, model, procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adult, female, Swiss Webster mice will be used in the experiments proposed. The non-lethal surgical excision mouse model will be used to study chronic infection as previously described. Mice will be anesthetized by intraperitoneal injection of sodium pentobarbital; backs shaved and a full-thickness, dorsal, 1.0 x 1.0 cm excisional skin wound to the level of panniculus muscle will be made. Wounds will be infected with approximately 10^5 colony forming units of bacteria and covered with a semipermeable polyurethane (OPSITE) dressing. Mice will be given warmed lactated ringers as fluid replacement and allowed to recover under warming lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise experimental details (strain, sex, anesthesia, surgical procedures, wound dimensions, inoculum size, dressings, post-op care) and cite prior use/validation of the model to justify its appropriateness for the study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for use of animals and sample size/power
rubrics_metrics.description: Although artificial skin models have been used for studying wound healing, there are currently no good in vitro models for evaluating the host response to wound infection. The numbers of animals to be used for the efficacy experiments are based on our experience of determining the minimum number of mice needed to generate statistically significant data. With our prior experience with this model, to power the study with a 85% confidence interval, a minimum of 9-12 animals will be needed for each experimental group (depending on the number of parameters being assessed). Smaller group sizes can often be used when larger effects are expected. However, until we know the expected variance in outcome, exact sample size estimates cannot be made. We have carefully tried to design the experiments so that data from as many parameters possible will be obtained from as few mice possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify why animals are necessary (lack of in vitro alternative), provide power/sample-size rationale and expected ranges (e.g., 9–12 per group for 85% CI), note uncertainty when variance is unknown, and describe design choices to minimize animal numbers (multiple assays per animal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Veterinary care, housing, and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals are housed in the centrally managed TTUHSC Animal Facility under the supervision of a staff vivarium director, a veterinarian (Dr. Scott Trasti), a staff of trained support personnel, which is overseen by the TTUHSC Animal Care Committee. TTUHSC is fully accredited by the AALAC. An Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee reviews all the proposals to ensure the ethical and humane treatment of animals. The vivarium follows the NIH Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (revised 1985) ... and all applicable government regulations ... and TTUHSC policies governing the care and use of laboratory animal. All physical plant construction, as well as plant maintenance, husbandry, and transportation, are in compliance with the Animal Welfare Act (PL89-544, PL91-579 and PL94-279).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document facility oversight, veterinary supervision, accreditation (AALAC), and compliance with federal regulations and institutional policies to demonstrate appropriate animal care infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to limit discomfort, distress, pain, and injury
rubrics_metrics.description: To alleviate discomfort, distress and pain, after surgery and during wound care, analgesics will be given (1-2% lidocaine (max dose of 10 mg/kg) + 0.25-0.5% bupivacaine in equal volume) twice daily (AM and PM) pre-emptively. Analgesics will also be given if there are signs of sickness; inactivity, sunken eyes, hunched posture, matted fur, abdominal vacuolization when handled. A mouse showing signs of morbidity (recumbent posture, labored breathing, unresponsiveness) will be euthanized. In addition, moist food within reach and additional bedding materials will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify analgesic agents/doses, schedule (preemptive and as-needed), welfare monitoring signs that trigger intervention, humane endpoints for euthanasia, and enrichment/supportive care measures (moist food, bedding) to reduce suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of euthanasia and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Euthanasia is carried out by intracardial injection of ‘Fatal Plus’, a method approved by the American Veterinary Medical Association Panel on Euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the exact euthanasia method and cite AVMA approval; provide rationale for choice if needed and ensure personnel competency/justification for the method selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table/breakdown of animal numbers by experimental group/timepoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1. Breakdown and numbers of mice to be used — lists Experimental Group, Data to be obtained, # of mice/group, # of repeats, # of PA strains tested, # of time points assessed, and Total number of mice. Example totals across aims and activities produce aggregate numbers (table entries for Specific Aim 1 and 3 are shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear tabular breakdown of animals per group, repeats, strains, time points, and totals for each specific aim and activity to demonstrate planning and to allow review of animal use justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical aspects: minimize animals and humane treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: We intend to use mice for experiments described in this study. We have conscientiously attempted to design our experiments to evaluate as many parameters per mouse as possible. Procedures to reduce discomfort, distress, pain, and injury have been put in place including the use of a preemptive analgesic. Mice used in these experiments will be treated humanely and in accordance with the protocol approved by the Animal Care and Use Committee at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (Lubbock, TX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate ethical commitment: minimize numbers via design, use preemptive analgesia, humane treatment, and adherence to approved protocols; reference committee approval to support ethical compliance.
